description: A hands-on first course in robotics: how robots sense, decide and move, from a single motor to a team-built mobile robot. Students wire motors and sensors on the hardware bench, program a microcontroller, tune feedback loops and finish with a robot challenge.
modelledOn: Siegwart, Nourbakhsh and Scaramuzza, Introduction to Autonomous Mobile Robots
Dudek and Jenkin, Computational Principles of Mobile Robotics
outcomes: Describe a robot as a sense-plan-act system and draw the block diagram of a given robot.
Select, drive and size DC, servo and stepper motors for a given load using PWM and an H-bridge.
Choose, calibrate and filter sensors, and convert raw readings to physical units.
Program a microcontroller with digital and analog I/O, timers, interrupts and state machines.
Implement and tune proportional and PID feedback controllers for speed, position and line following.
Build, test and demonstrate a mobile robot as part of a team, documenting design decisions and safety measures.

units.title: What a robot is and its components
topics: Definitions and history; types of robot (arm, mobile, legged, aerial) and levels of autonomy
Components of a robot: structure, actuators, sensors, controller and power, and the sense-plan-act loop
Degrees of freedom, joints, workspace and a first look at the geometry of a two-link arm
Robots in Africa: farm spraying, mining inspection, medical drone delivery and the safety and ethics questions they raise
Electronics for robots: voltage, current, Ohm's law, power budget and battery selection

units.title: Actuators and motors
topics: The brushed DC motor: torque, speed, back-EMF and stall current
H-bridge drivers and PWM speed control; reversing direction
Hobby servo motors: pulse widths, position control and range limits
Stepper motors: full, half and micro-stepping, steps per revolution, open-loop positioning
Gearboxes, the torque-speed trade-off, wheel size and motor power sizing
Motor driver protection: flyback diodes, current limits and electrical noise

units.title: Sensors and signal conditioning
topics: Sensor characteristics: range, resolution, accuracy, precision, noise and response time
Light, line and proximity sensing: infrared reflectance, ultrasonic ranging, time of flight
Quadrature encoders: counting ticks, speed estimation and wheel odometry
Inertial sensing: accelerometer, gyroscope, IMU and gyro drift
Analog conditioning: voltage dividers, op-amp amplifiers, the ADC and quantisation error
Digital filtering: moving average, exponential low-pass and median filters for spikes

units.title: Microcontroller programming
topics: Microcontroller architecture (AVR): GPIO, timers, ADC and interrupts
Digital I/O, analog read and PWM output: buttons, LEDs and motor speed
Reading sensors, serial debugging and calibration routines
Timers and interrupts: non-blocking loops and encoder interrupt handlers
Behaviour as a finite state machine in code
A single-board computer in the loop: serial, I2C and MQTT messaging between boards

units.title: Basic feedback control
topics: Open loop versus closed loop; setpoint, error and actuator saturation
On-off control with hysteresis
Proportional control and steady-state error
PID control: integral windup, derivative kick and discrete-time implementation
Step-response tuning: rise time, overshoot, settling time and the Ziegler-Nichols rules
Line following and wall following as feedback problems

units.title: Mobile robot motion and navigation
topics: Differential-drive kinematics: wheel speeds to forward and turning velocity
Odometry and dead reckoning; how errors accumulate
Reactive obstacle avoidance and Braitenberg-style behaviours
Grid maps and path search: breadth-first search and A-star on an occupancy grid
Behaviour-based control: subsumption and behaviour arbitration

units.title: Building a mobile robot
topics: Requirements, chassis design, wheel placement and centre of mass
Wiring, power distribution and subsystem testing
Integration, test plans and debugging with logs
Safety: emergency stop, fail-safe states and battery handling

units.title: Team robot challenge
topics: Challenge specification, scoring rules and project planning
Team roles, version control and design documentation
Demonstration, run analysis and failure review
Reflection: reliability, cost, ethics and local impact of the robot

schedule.title: What is a robot?
schedule.exercise: Draw the sense-plan-act block diagram of a robot vacuum and of a spraying drone, list their sensors and actuators, and compute the battery life of a 2000 mAh pack at a given load.

tasks.title: Wire an LED and a resistor on the bench, measure current against Ohm's law for three resistor values, and record the battery drain of each
Draw a sense-plan-act block diagram of a farm irrigation robot naming each sensor, actuator and the controller, and link signals between them
Plot the reachable workspace of a two-link arm with given link lengths and joint limits and decide if a target point is reachable

schedule.title: DC motors, H-bridges and servos
schedule.exercise: Estimate the stall current and no-load speed of a motor from its datasheet, and explain how PWM duty cycle changes average voltage in an H-bridge.

tasks.title: Drive a DC motor through an H-bridge from a microcontroller pin and change speed with PWM duty at 25, 50 and 100 percent
Attach a servo, sweep it from 0 to 180 degrees with pulse widths from 1 to 2 ms, and record the real angle at five widths
Fit a motor speed-versus-voltage line from measured data, estimate the back-EMF constant and predict speed at an unseen voltage

schedule.title: Steppers, gears and driver protection
schedule.exercise: Size a motor and gearbox so that a 1 kg robot climbs a 10 degree ramp at 0.3 m/s, showing torque, speed and power numbers.

tasks.title: Drive a stepper through 200 full steps and 400 half steps, count revolutions and compute steps per revolution and the angle error
Compute the required wheel torque for a robot on a ramp, choose a gear ratio from a table and plot torque against speed
Find the fault in a motor circuit that resets the microcontroller when the motor starts, and fix it with a flyback diode and decoupling

schedule.title: Sensor characteristics, ranging and encoders
schedule.exercise: Compare an infrared and an ultrasonic distance sensor on range, resolution and noise, and compute wheel odometry for a robot that travels a measured square.

tasks.title: Measure distance with an ultrasonic sensor at 10 known distances and plot reading against truth to estimate error and range limit
Count encoder ticks while a wheel turns one revolution, compute distance travelled and compare it with a ruler measurement
Collect 200 readings of a distance sensor, compute the mean, standard deviation and resolution, and report the sensor accuracy

schedule.title: Inertial sensing, conditioning and filtering
schedule.exercise: Show with a short dataset how a gyroscope drifts, pick the cut-off of a low-pass filter for a noisy signal, and compute ADC resolution in millivolts.

tasks.title: Read a potentiometer with the 10-bit ADC, convert counts to volts and compute the quantisation step for the 5 V range
Filter a noisy sensor trace with moving-average and exponential filters, and compare lag and noise reduction for three window sizes
Integrate a gyro rate trace to estimate heading, measure the drift over 60 s, and correct it by fusing with a compass reading

schedule.title: Programming the microcontroller
schedule.exercise: Write a program that reads a button, an analog light sensor and a distance sensor, prints readings over serial and lights an LED when a threshold is crossed.

tasks.title: Program a button to toggle an LED and a potentiometer to dim a second LED with PWM, then verify behaviour on the bench
Calibrate a light sensor by reading it in light and dark conditions and map its range onto 0 to 100 percent in code
Write C code that configures a timer to output a 1 kHz PWM and verify its period with a counter-based measurement routine

schedule.title: Timers, interrupts and state machines
schedule.exercise: Convert a blocking blink-and-read program into a non-blocking one, and draw the state machine of a robot that waits, drives and stops at an obstacle.

tasks.title: Replace delay calls with a millis-based scheduler so that an LED blinks at 2 Hz while a sensor is read every 100 ms
Step through a three-state drive-turn-stop machine in the visualiser and record the state sequence for a given sensor input stream
Send sensor readings from a microcontroller to a single-board computer by MQTT and plot the live values on a dashboard

schedule.title: Open loop, on-off and proportional control
schedule.exercise: Compare open-loop and closed-loop motor speed under a load change, and compute the steady-state error of a proportional controller for three gains.

tasks.title: Build an on-off controller with hysteresis for a heater or fan and show on a plot how the band changes switching frequency
Simulate proportional control of a motor speed model for gains 1, 5 and 20 and tabulate steady-state error and overshoot
Simulate a motor with actuator saturation under open and closed loop, then identify which gain makes the response unstable

schedule.title: PID tuning and line following
schedule.exercise: Tune a PID controller from a measured step response using a rule of thumb, and explain integral windup with a saturating actuator.

tasks.title: Read rise time, overshoot and settling time from a given step response plot and compare two tuning candidates against a spec
Program a line follower with proportional steering on two reflectance sensors and complete a test track in under a time limit
Implement a discrete PID with anti-windup and derivative filtering, and compare it with a plain PID on a saturating plant

schedule.title: Kinematics, odometry and avoidance
schedule.exercise: Compute the pose of a differential-drive robot after a given sequence of wheel speeds, and quantify how an encoder error of 1 percent grows over 10 m.

tasks.title: Convert left and right wheel speeds into forward and turning velocity and plot the path for five wheel-speed pairs
Dead-reckon a square path of 1 m sides with a simulated wheel slip error and report the position error at the end of each lap
Program obstacle avoidance with two ultrasonic sensors, and record the robot trajectory when it meets a wall at three angles

schedule.title: Path search and behaviour-based control
schedule.exercise: Run breadth-first and A-star search on a grid map of a warehouse, count the cells expanded by each, and arrange three behaviours by priority.

tasks.title: Run breadth-first search on a 10x10 grid map with obstacles in the visualiser and record the path length and number of cells expanded
Compare A-star with two heuristics against breadth-first on the same map and explain which expands fewer cells and why
Implement a subsumption controller with avoid, wander and seek-light behaviours and test the arbitration against a simulated sensor stream

schedule.title: Build and test the robot
schedule.exercise: Draw the wiring diagram and test plan of your team robot, with a power budget, a safety checklist and a plan to test each subsystem before integration.

tasks.title: Wire motors, sensors and a battery to the controller with separate power rails, then power-up test each subsystem in order
Log sensor and motor values during a test run, find why the robot veers left, and correct the cause with calibration
Draw a fault-tree for a robot that does not stop on command, and add an emergency stop and fail-safe default that remove the branch

schedule.title: Team robot challenge
schedule.exercise: Demonstrate the robot on a set challenge, submit a design report with plan, test results and failure review, and reflect on cost, reliability and local use.

tasks.title: Draw a Gantt chart for a 4-week robot challenge with tasks, owners and dependencies, and mark the critical path
Run the robot on the challenge course five times, record time and errors for each run, and report the mean and the main failure
Put the team code under version control with branches for sensing, control and navigation, and merge them into a tagged release
